metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton - Facing 3-to-4-month absence
metadata.description: Thornton is slated to undergo surgery later this week to address the dislocated left ankle he sustained in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders and is facing an expected recovery timeline of 3-to-4 weeks, Matt Zenitz of CBSSports.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Depending how quickly Thornton bounces back from surgery, Zenitz notes that the speedy receiver could have a small chance at returning late in the regular season or during the playoffs. The injury is nonetheless a devastating development for Thornton, who had turned in perhaps the best performance of his career -- a five-catch, 111-yard, two-touchdown effort on eight targets -- before going down with the gruesome ankle injury at the end of a 55-yard reception with just under four minutes left in the fourth quarter. In Thornton's absence, the Chiefs could call upon Xavier Worthy to run more vertical routes, and Kansas City may also have interest in a reunion with Tyreek Hill (knee), who is expected to sign a deal with a team within the next few days.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton (ankle) to miss 12-to-16 weeks
metadata.description: Chiefs WR Tyquan Thorntonwill miss 12-16 weeks.
metadata.analysis: Thornton is having surgery "within the week" and is likely to miss the rest of the season. Xavier Worthy should be among the players to see more opportunity in his place.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton to Have Surgery, Facing 12-to-16-Week Recovery
metadata.description: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton (ankle) is expected to miss 12 to 16 weeks after undergoing extensive testing Monday. Ian Rapoport reported that Thornton will have surgery within the next week for the dislocated left ankle he suffered during Sunday's win over the Las Vegas Raiders. There is a real chance he could return late in the season or during the playoffs, though that will depend on how his recovery progresses. Thornton was having his best game of the year before the injury, catching five of eight targets for 111 yards and two touchdowns. He has 11 receptions for 219 yards and two scores through four games. The timetable takes Thornton out of the fantasy picture for the foreseeable future, while Kansas City will have to replace one of its top deep threats as he begins a lengthy recovery.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton catches two TDs, injures ankle in Week 4
metadata.description: Tyquan Thornton caught five of his eight targets for 111 yards and two touchdowns in a 30-27 win over the Raiders in Week 4.
metadata.analysis: Thornton led the Chiefs in receiving with Rashee Rice departing early after a hamstring injury. Thornton also suffered an injury as he suffered what appeared to be a serious left ankle injury in the fourth quarter. Look for the Chiefs to update his status in the next few days.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton - Out indefinitely due to dislocated ankle
metadata.description: Thornton (ankle) is out indefinitely after dislocating his ankle during Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders, Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Thornton had his dislocated ankle put back into place by doctors Sunday and flew home with the team, but he's facing an extended absence due to the injury he sustained in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win in Vegas. He scored twice before getting injured at the end of a 55-yard catch, which brought Thornton up to five receptions for 111 yards on eight targets. Thornton will undergo a full evaluation of the injured left ankle Monday morning.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton - Carted with obvious ankle injury
metadata.description: Thornton exited Sunday's game agains the Raiders with a left ankle injury and will not return.
metadata.analysis: Thornton was injured at the end of a long catch in the fourth quarter when he was tackled from behind, as the defender fell on his ankle. It was an obviously serious injury, with Thornton's foot pointing the wrong direction. He was put in a cast and carted off the field. Thornton was having a career game in Las Vegas, catching five of eight targets for 111 yards and two touchdowns prior to his injury. Jalen Royals is next up at wideout alongside Xavier Worthy after Rashee Rice (hamstring) left with an injury earlier in the day Sunday.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton Dislocates His Ankle, Ruled Out Indefinitely
metadata.description: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton (ankle) suffered a dislocated ankle during Sunday's Week 4 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL.com. Thornton hauled in a deep pass, and the initial celebration quickly turned to extreme concern once the severity of his injury became evident. He was quickly taken to the hospital, where doctors fixed his dislocated ankle and gave him permission to fly back to Kansas City with the team. It was encouraging to see the quick turnaround to get him back in Kansas City, but it won't mean much this year. After all, the ankle injury is most likely going to be season-ending. Between the injuries to Thornton and Rashee Rice (hamstring), Kansas City's receiver room is suddenly shorthanded and may look to bolster the position group via free agency or trade.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton Suffers "Gruesome" Injury Vs. Raiders
metadata.description: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton (leg) suffered a "gruesome" leg injury in a Week 4 matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports. Warren added that Thornton was carted off of the field. It appears to be a lower-leg injury for Thornton. Following a 55-yard gain on a reception in the fourth quarter, Thornton attempted to stand up and immediately went back down to the ground. Thornton was having a strong game with five receptions for 111 yards and two touchdowns before exiting. With Thornton out likely out and fellow wideout Rashee Rice also getting hurt earlier in the game, the Chiefs will rely on wide receiver Xavier Worthy, tight end Travis Kelce, running back Kenneth Walker III and others in the passing game

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton Could Be A Valuable Deep Threat Option Against Vegas
metadata.description: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton will face the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4. Thornton has been the de facto deep threat option for quarterback Patrick Mahomes this season and his skill set may be necessary against a divisional opponent this week. Thornton recently caught two passes for 22 yards in the 24-10 win over the Miami Dolphins, but flashed more upside in the previous week with a closer game. In a 33-30 overtime win against the Indianapolis Colts, Thornton had four catches for 86 yards with a long catch of 45 yards in the contest. The Raiders defense has been stingy to start the season, so a big play or two may be necessary to take the top off the defense. Thornton is ranked WR70 in our RotoBaller Week 4 PPR rankings, making him a desperate flex option. Fantasy managers starting Thornton this week will need to hope for a deep catch or a score to salvage his day.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton - Catches two targets in win
metadata.description: Thornton caught both of his targets for 22 yards in the Chiefs' 24-10 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Thornton saw less attention from Patrick Mahomes than in the Chiefs' Week 2 overtime win over the Colts. Thornton saw 45 percent of the team's offensive snaps in the contest, down from 59 percent and 68 percent in the prior weeks. The lack of downfield targets and attention to the No. 3 wide receiver could be a result of a strong run game that ran out the clock against a trailing opponent.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton catches two passes in Week 3
metadata.description: Tyquan Thornton caught both of his targets for 22 yards in the Chiefs' 24-10 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 3.
metadata.analysis: Thornton has seen minimal involvement in the Kansas City offense to begin the season, posting two targets or less in two of the first three games. The wideout remains difficult to trust ahead of a Week 4 contest against the Las Vegas Raiders.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton is a Deep League Play for Week 3
metadata.description: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton is coming off a solid performance against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 2. Thornton hauled in all four of his targets for 86 yards in the overtime victory. The 26-year-old was held without a catch in the opener, but now he appears to be getting on the same page as quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Thornton is currently the third wide receiver in this offense, but is unlikely to provide weekly value. He'll head into a favorable matchup against the Miami Dolphins in Week 3. His role is probably too inconsistent at the moment to trust in most fantasy formats.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton - Catches all four targets in win
metadata.description: Thornton caught all four of his targets for 86 yards in Sunday's 33-30 overtime win against the Colts.
metadata.analysis: Thornton and quarterback Patrick Mahomes have struggled to get on the same page since before Mahomes' ACL injury. The quarterback-receiver duo missed no such deep balls Sunday, connecting each time Thornton was thrown to. The wide receiver played 47 of the Chiefs' 80 offensive snaps in the contest.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton productive in OT win Sunday
metadata.description: Tyquan Thornton caught four passes for 86 yards in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
metadata.analysis: Thornton looked great on Sunday night, leading Kansas City's wideouts with 86 yards on four catches. His production as a downfield threat helped lead the Chiefs to a close overtime win over the Colts, although for fantasy purposes he doesn't project to be of much use for the foreseeable future.

metadata.title: Expect More From Tyquan Thornton In Week 2 Vs. Colts
metadata.description: With the Kansas City Chiefs playing the Indianapolis Colts in Week 2, look for wide receiver Tyquan Thornton to establish a role for himself in the offense after failing to do so in Week 1's win over the Denver Broncos. Thornton saw just one target and did not catch a pass in Week 1's route. Still behind Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy on the depth chart, expect Thornton to establish himself more as the No. 3 wide receiver target for the Chiefs. The Colts were blitzed by the Ravens in the opener and allowed 354 passing yards to Baltimore. The Chiefs have an explosive offense with many mouths to feed, including running backs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson, along with tight end Travis Kelce. Despite the slow start, look for Thornton to get more involved in Week 2 in what could be another route for the Chiefs.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton - No catches in Week 1
metadata.description: Thornton didn't catch his only target during Monday night's 31-10 win over the Broncos.
metadata.analysis: Thornton was on the field for 47 of the team's 69 offensive snaps, but he failed to leave his mark on the contest. The wide receiver is used primarily as a deep threat, and as a result, his production will likely vary significantly from week to week.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton silent in win Monday
metadata.description: Tyquan Thornton failed to catch his single target in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
metadata.analysis: Thornton showed a lot of promise in Kansas City's offense last year, but he is off to a rough start in 2026, being held without a catch in the team's first game of the season. He may get more involved as QB Patrick Mahomes II continues to knock the rust off after missing significant time with a knee injury, but fantasy managers shouldn't count on him being a consistent contributor at any point this season.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton's Fantasy Appeal Slipping Away
metadata.description: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton is trending down in fantasy football ahead of the 2026 NFL season. While Thornton remains in the No. 3 spot on the depth chart for now, he'll likely lose his grasp on that role by midseason. He's already behind Rashee Rice, Travis Kelce, and Xavier Worthy in the passing game order, and soon, he could also be surpassed by up-and-coming rookie Cyrus Allen. The fifth-round pick out of Cincinnati reportedly had a great training camp, earning the trust of quarterback Patrick Mahomes and the coaching staff. Thornton, on the other hand, has struggled to emerge as a consistent threat in the passing game throughout his four seasons in the league. Now heading into Year 5, Thornton has yet to finish higher than WR81 in a single season.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton - One catch to close preseason
metadata.description: Thornton secured one of two targets for 11 yards in the Chiefs' 9-9 preseason tie with the Seahawks on Friday.
metadata.analysis: The fifth-year pro drew a start and matched his one catch from preseason Week 2, albeit while gaining six more yards than in that performance. Thornton somewhat revived his career during his 2025 Chiefs debut campaign by averaging 23.1 yards per reception on his 19 catches and recording three scoring grabs, and he projects to open the season in the prominent role of No. 3 receiver in what should be a dynamic air attack.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton - Returns to practice after Tuesday exit
metadata.description: Thornton (hamstring) is participating in Wednesday's practice, Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Thornton left Tuesday's practice on a cart after tweaking his hamstring, though his presence on the field a day later suggests that his early exit may have been precautionary more than anything. He's donning full pads Wednesday, so Thornton doesn't look as though he will be limited in the session.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton Returns From Hamstring Injury
metadata.description: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton (hamstring) is back out at training camp practice on Wednesday in pads after leaving Tuesday's practice early with a hamstring injury, according to Matt McMullen of the team's official website. Thornton was carted to the locker room with a left-hamstring injury, but it turned out to be nothing serious, and he could be available to play in Saturday's preseason game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. If fully healthy for the start of the 2026 regular season, the 26-year-old figures to be KC's WR3 behind Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy, although rookie Cyrus Allen has been pushing for a bigger role with a strong training camp this summer. Even with both Rice and Worthy missing time last year, Thornton only caught 19 passes for 438 yards and three touchdowns in 14 games in his first year with the team. The former second-rounder in 2022 from Baylor can stretch the field and produce big plays, but he is too inconsistent and won't have enough weekly targets to be worth targeting in 12-team fantasy leagues.

metadata.title: Tyquan Thornton suffers hamstring strain
metadata.description: Chiefs WR Tyquan Thornton suffered a hamstring strain at practice on Tuesday.
metadata.analysis: Thornton was carted off the field during practice with the injury. It is unclear how long he'll be sidelined for.
